 FILE — A sign directs people to the polling place at Hartford City Hall on Tuesday, March 26, 2024 – the first day of early voting in Connecticut. Credit: Jamil Ragland / CTNewsJunkie 
 Nearly 32,000 more voters cast an early in-person ballot Monday, bringing the total after eight of the 14 early voting days to 231,577, according to numbers from Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas’ office.
 Of the 31,717 early votes cast in person on Oct. 26, 14,478 of them were cast by registered Democrats, and 6,553 by Republicans. Unaffiliated voters, who make up the largest block of registered voters, cast 10,295 votes and those registered with a minor party cast another 391.
 Note that these counts are unofficial and subject to change as all municipalities do not report on the same schedule.
 The state also has received a total of 38,537 absentee ballots. That total includes 19,947 from Democrats, 7,048 from Republicans, 11,041 from unaffiliated voters and 501 from minor party members. Including the absentee ballots, there now have been 270,114 votes cast in advance of Election Day, Nov. 3.
 Democrats, who represent 35.6% of the electorate, have cast 51.9% of the early in-person votes and 51.7% of the absentee ballots. Republicans (21.5% of registered voters) represented 17.8% of the early voters and 18.2% of the absentees. The unaffiliated (41.4% of the electorate) have cast 28.9% of the early votes and 28.6% of the absentee ballots.
 Statewide, 2,058 voters have used same-day registration to cast an in-person vote.
 Early voting continues through Nov. 1.
